about: Relations between the powers, their monthly events, commissions and contract terms. Hand-written from the owner's foundational lore (docs/lore/foundational_lore.md); read by scripts/diplomacy.gd. Relations run from -100 to 100 and drift back toward these starting values; bands: war at -82 or below (an armistice returns above -60), hostile below -30, cool below -5, cordial from 20, allied from 50.

concord.title: Concord reserve commission
concord.text: A reserve commission in the Hesperian Concord's navy: Concord contracts, Concord pay, and the Concord's wars become yours.

directorate.title: Directorate auxiliary warrant
directorate.text: A warrant as an auxiliary of the Vargan Directorate's fleet. Raiders who hurt Concord shipping are tolerated; captains who serve are paid.

pacific.title: Federation scouting charter
pacific.text: A charter from the Halcyon Federation to scout and escort among the island chains. It pays to keep the balance.

combine.title: Combine security contract
combine.text: A retainer with the Meridian Combine's security fleets. Everything is a contract; reliable contractors are retained.

republic.title: Tarsene letter of marque
republic.text: A letter of marque from the Tarsene Free Republic against Directorate shipping. The paper is only as good as the guns behind it.

freeport.title: Syndicate letter of marque
freeport.text: A Syndicate letter-broker's marque against Concord shipping. The Syndicate considers you family, until you become a liability.

ombria.title: Protectorate coastal warrant
ombria.text: A warrant from the junta in Sefira to guard the Ombrian shore. The pay comes from Strelsk, and everyone knows it.

isles.title: League reef charter
isles.text: A charter from the Outer Isles League to keep the raiders off their reefs. Small pay, long memories, and harbours that are always glad to see you.

events.text: Hardliners carry the vote on the Concord's Admiralty Board. Patrols off the Strelsk Sounds are doubled.
Concord moderates win the argument in Calder Roads: another round of mutual ruin is not worth the Gate. Patrols are told to keep their distance.
The Concord demands "responsible control" of the Tarsene Gate. Tarsa refuses, and says so from the shore batteries.
The Tarsene Free Republic, desperate for friends, opens its harbours to Syndicate traders and Federation merchantmen.
A Combine tanker convoy is seen bunkering Directorate submarines in the Monsoon Ocean. Kotaraya calls it ordinary commerce.
The Meridian Combine sells the Concord a squadron of new escorts, cash on delivery.
Directorate submarines are sighted beyond the Throat, heading for the Monsoon trade. The Entente calls it a breach of the armistice.
Amakura signs a fishing and trade convention with Strelsk. The Federation prefers balance to alliances.
Concord and Federation carriers exercise together off the Arcs. Strelsk protests.
The Concord boards Syndicate blockade-runners off Port Saffron. The freeports promise long memories.
Halvard mediators convene talks aboard an icebreaker in the Skarn Passages, where the armistice was signed.
A Directorate garrison on a "temporarily" occupied island in the Halcyon reefs refuses to withdraw.
A Directorate scientist defects to the Concord, with papers on guided weapons. Every intelligence service on the map takes notice.
Raiders sheltering in the freeports strike Combine shipping in the Saffron Sea. Kotaraya blames Port Saffron.
Strikes in the Ombrian ports. The junta in Sefira asks Strelsk for more advisers; some officers ask Calder Roads for something else.
The Protectorate's gunboats stop a Tarsene merchantman in the Cradle Sea and send her home without her cargo.
Raiders strike the reef villages of the Outer Isles. The League asks the Concord for escorts and the freeports for the raiders' names.
The Outer Isles League and the Halcyon Federation sign a coaling agreement. Amakura still hopes they will join the Federation one day.

coalitions.about: The wartime coalitions of the Meridian War (the owner's lore). When a member goes to war with a member of the other coalition, its allies (relations 50 or better) join at once; members merely cordial (20 or better) join half the time. Each power's own relations still decide.

sieges.about: In a war, about every 25 days one side may move on a port of the other: the defender's nearest harbour to the attacker's own, never a capital. The odds come from the fleets within reach of the port (about 900 units), weighted by each navy's quality (the lore: the Concord is still the strongest blue-water navy), against the harbour's own defences and garrison. Occupied ports stay occupied after an armistice.
